entries.subject: Schenk/LPI 2020 oumap-cyl-180180.cub
entries.finding: Included as Monochrome. Updated control network and native numeric samples make it preferable to the older display-texture map. The release supplies photometrically corrected imagery; preserved shadows and seams are disclosed.

entries.subject: Schenk/LPI 2020 oumapZlimb.cub
entries.finding: Excluded as an Elevation dataset. These are sparse digitized limb profiles, not extended surface elevation coverage. The author warns that their older control network may displace them by several degrees. They must not be expanded into neighboring terrain or treated as a registered full-surface DEM.
entries.revisitWhen: A released Oberon topographic reconstruction provides extended measured coverage registered to the selected mosaic; sparse limb values alone cannot fill that gap.

entries.subject: Schenk and Moore 2023 topography overview and 2020 source paper
entries.finding: Supporting scientific context. The authors explicitly describe the lack of extended topography on Oberon and Umbriel, confirming why this package has no Elevation dataset. Paper figures are not substitutes for measured raster coverage.

entries.subject: JPL simulator Oberon texture, 1440 × 720, 4 pixels/degree
entries.finding: Superseded as a display source. It derives from USGS/Voyager grayscale imagery, but does not provide the selected release's revised control metadata and floating-point source values. Its nominal pixel count is not evidence of more native detail. No duplicate dataset is added.
entries.revisitWhen: A better controlled JPL release provides observed detail or coverage beyond the selected Schenk mosaic.

entries.subject: PDS Voyager 2 Uranus ISS EDR archive
entries.finding: Underlying observation archive, excluded from this presentation in favor of the already corrected and controlled release. Raw frames would require a separate radiometric and pointing reconstruction; PDS warns about errors in original emission/incidence metadata.
entries.revisitWhen: A Oberon observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Voyager C2683625 / C2683627 / C2683629 color reconstruction
entries.finding: The 2026-09-07 trial used calibrated GEOMED CLEAR C2683625, VIOLET C2683627 and GREEN C2683629 (about 5 km/pixel, roughly 300-pixel disc), following the Helfenstein photometry route. Final image-space RMS was 0.55, 0.86 and 1.07 pixels respectively. Despite bounded Lunar-Lambert correction and missing unstable limb samples, mounted color views were softer than Monochrome, with chromatic fringes and a visible coverage transition. This trial did not qualify a second dataset.
entries.revisitWhen: A sharper reconstruction with independently validated inter-band registration removes the chromatic fringes and visible coverage transition without borrowing monochrome detail.

entries.subject: JPL PIA00034 color disc
entries.finding: Excluded from mapped datasets. The published disc reconstructs color from violet, clear and green filters; the press image alone does not supply a calibrated, registered surface product or new coverage.
entries.revisitWhen: A Oberon observation or controlled reconstruction demonstrates useful native surface detail, body-fixed geometry and independent registration beyond the cited sampling or coverage limits.

entries.subject: Geologic map manuscript catalog
entries.finding: Unresolved interpretive candidate. The catalog records a manuscript color plate but supplies no downloadable qualified geospatial units or source projection/coverage metadata. It is not used as a scientific raster.
entries.revisitWhen: The catalog’s linked manuscript data become downloadable with geospatial units, projection, coverage and reuse terms.

entries.subject: Voyager 2 ISS green/violet/ultraviolet color frames
entries.finding: 3 GEOMED frames in 1 complete sets (21.7 km per pixel) placed by limb fit and mosaic registration supply the Voyager color dataset. Whole-disc violet/green and ultraviolet/green are tied to Bell and McCord (1991) Fig. 2 (0.935, 0.915); the archive calibration gives 0.870 and 0.921. No phase normalisation; the north stays unavailable.

entries.subject: Photometric law for the lighting overlays
entries.finding: Hapke law of Helfenstein, Hillier, Weitz and Veverka, read in their summary in NASA's Reports of Planetary Geology and Geophysics Program 1989 (TM-4210, pages 230 and 231); the Icarus paper (1991) was not read. They fitted Hapke's 1986 model to Voyager imaging and Earth-based photometry. Table I, global average, clear filter (0.48 micrometres): single-scattering albedo 0.41, asymmetry -0.29, roughness 21 degrees, with the opposition surge fixed at h = 0.007 and B0 = 1.03. Flood-lit, the limb is 0.97 of the centre; the narrow opposition surge puts the point under the Sun at 0.74 of that centre at 1 degree phase and 0.55 at 10 degrees, so frames with Shadows on are dim against the flood-lit view. The table also prints green and violet rows and three terrains; one clear-filter global row lights every channel and terrain here. It is second class: the report prints no phase or emission range. The phase range 18 to 148 degrees is the span of the resolved Voyager 2 frames the PDS node lists, and the emission limit 84.9 degrees comes from the outermost pixel of the frame the report names as its finest (FDS 26836.25, 6.130 km per pixel); both are derived here. Helfenstein, Veverka and Thomas (1988) fitted Hapke models to whole-disc photometry of the five moons; that paper could not be read. Thomas and Veverka's 1986 summary gives a Minnaert k near 0.7 for Oberon at 33 degrees phase, one phase only. The same check that Titania passes, run on 2026-10-05 on two calibrated clear frames at 19 and 39 degrees phase (FDS 26809.04 and 26836.23), gives lunar-Lambert weights of 0.60 and 0.39 where this law gives 0.74 and 0.62; a Minnaert k of 0.7 at 33 degrees corresponds to 0.54. Two frames of a disc with uneven albedo do not outweigh two published fits, so the law stands, with this noted.
entries.revisitWhen: The fitted phase and emission ranges are read in the Icarus paper, or a per-filter law is wanted for the color dataset.

entries.subject: Shared sphere bank lighting (Lambert with a 0.35 flood floor and 0.05 ambient term, adapted from OpenSpace)
entries.finding: Replaced by the Hapke law of Helfenstein, Hillier, Weitz and Veverka (1989); Oberon now bakes its own bank.
entries.revisitWhen: Nothing: an authored limb is not reopened once a published law exists.

entries.subject: Surface map left edge after the raster lane change
entries.finding: The raster lane writes this map from 0° E, but surface-map.json still declared the retired atlas's 180° E left edge, so the globe, labels and status-bar longitude were half a turn from the imagery. Read through its georeferenced source, the prepared normal map correlates 0.95 from 0° E and 0.16 from 180° E. The declaration is now 0° E, and preparation refuses a declared edge the source contradicts.
